metadata.title: Random But True: The Passport Printed With the Photographer's Watermark
metadata.caption:
Look closely at pages 34 and 35 of the Syrian passport and you'll find "WASEEM ASMAR PHOTOGRAPHY" printed right into the artwork.

The image is Souq al-Hamidiyah, the historic covered market in Damascus. The photo was apparently pulled from the internet without anyone removing the photographer's watermark first.

Here's the part most people sharing this online are getting wrong: it isn't a new blunder. The watermarked photo has been on Syrian biometric passports for years, and the photographer himself spoke about it publicly back in 2024.

An accidental photo credit - printed over and over, and hiding in plain sight the whole time.

Comment if you've ever spotted something like this on an official document.
